content.introduction: The stock market under Trump's administration saw significant growth, driven by corporate earnings and tax cuts, despite geopolitical risks. The S&P 500 climbed over 25% since the 2024 election, with quick recoveries from pullbacks. Trump's numerous trades have sparked debate about potential insider influence.
body: [](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.usbank.com/content/usbank/us/en/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html&title=Stocks+Under+the+Trump+Administration%3A+What+is+Driving+Markets+in+2026%3F+%7C+U.S.+Bank&summary=See+how+tariffs%2C+tax+cuts%2C+oil+prices%2C+and+earnings+are+shaping+the+stock+market+under+Trump+in+2026+and+what+investors+should+watch+next.&media=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.usbank.com%2Fcontent%2Fdam%2Fusbank%2Fen%2Fimages%2Fphotos%2Fwealth-management%2Fphoto-white-house-exterior-close-16x9.jpg). Since the 2024 presidential election, the S&P 500’s total return climbed more than 25% as of April 20, 2026, despite meaningful volatility along the way.[2](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_e4) “Investors have overcome concerns about geopolitical conflict and trade announcements and focused on fundamental strength, namely corporate earnings growth,” says Bill Merz, head of capital markets research for U.S. Bank Asset Management Group. S&P 500 companies increased fourth-quarter 2025 revenue by 9.2% and earnings by 13.4%, while first-quarter results are exceeding analyst expectations of 9.6% revenue growth and 13.0% earnings growth.[2](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_c93) Those fundamentals help explain why investors have continued to buy stocks despite higher oil prices, tariff uncertainty and persistent geopolitical risk. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act ([OBBBA](https://www.usbank.com/wealth-management/financial-perspectives/financial-planning/the-real-impact-of-the-tax-cuts-and-jobs-act.html)) lowered corporate and individual taxes, and federal tax refunds were running approximately $47 billion higher than in 2025 through April 24.[4](https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/stock-market-under-trump.html#footnote_region_c83b) Earlier Federal Reserve rate cuts also helped support borrowing and spending, giving investors another reason to maintain a constructive market view.

* Yet, the market has been more successful under the second Trump term than during other presidencies in recovering quicker than historical trends, data from CFRA Research shows. * Trump has been the dominating force behind the S&P 500's five best and five worst days since he took office in 2025, as revealed by Fundstrat. When it comes to S&P 500 pullbacks of 5% to 9.9% from its peak, the two that have occurred since early 2025 have reversed faster than the median of 34 days, according to CFRA Research. The most recent recovery in Trump's second term — when the S&P 500 bounced back from a 9.1% decline in only 16 calendar days — was one of the speediest since World War II, tying for ninth fastest, CFRA found. Investors have been so fixated on announcements out of the White House that Trump has been the main driver of the market's best — and worst — five days since his return to office, Fundstrat data shows.

President Donald Trump’s latest [financial disclosure](https://extapps2.oge.gov/201/Presiden.nsf/PAS+Index/405E4EC4E27BE8D185258DF7002DD1C0/%24FILE/Trump%2C%20Donald%20J.-05.08.2026-278T(2).pdf) has drawn scrutiny for its astonishing scale: 3,711 trades, almost entirely in shares of companies across America, including many whose fortunes can turn on federal policy. Collectively, they constitute an [unprecedented burst](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-14/trump-bought-nvidia-boeing-microsoft-in-flurry-of-transactions) of stock-market activity by a sitting president that has fueled fascination among the day-trading masses and prompted detractors to warn of insider-dealing. On Tuesday, Vice President JD Vance said the notion the president was trading from the Oval Office was “[absurd](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-19/trump-refrains-from-trading-his-own-stocks-vance-says).”. Elizabeth Warren, a Democratic senator from Massachusetts, [decried](https://www.warren.senate.gov/newsroom/videos/watch/donald-trump-made-more-than-3700-trades-this-year) “trades on companies that the Trump administration influenced with its own policies,” citing the purchase of $1 million of [Nvidia](https://fortune.com/company/nvidia/) Corp. For instance, the filing shows an unsolicited purchase of between $1 million and $5 million of [Apple](https://fortune.com/company/apple/) Inc. stock in early March, about a week before Trump publicly praised the company’s Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook.
